source.description:
PROBLEM: voidObligation mutates the durable obligation journal before proving resolving-evidence storage exists. Order today: private append() persists to journal (src/obligation/index.ts L341-345), THEN opts.evidence absence throws, THEN evidence.append would run. Caller without an evidence journal ends in: obligation state voided-on-journal, resolving evidence absent, caller observed failure - exactly the unsafe state the two-journal review rule targets. PR #100 added load-time reconcileOnLoad detection of voided_without_evidence (L320-339): necessary recovery backstop, does not make the original mutation order correct.

SUCCESS: Evidence-store precondition validated BEFORE any durable mutation: if store is missing/unusable => typed error, ZERO journal events written anywhere. If evidence append fails after the void event did persist, the defined recovery protocol applies and surfaces via the existing reconciliationReport on load; protocol documented inline where implemented.

SCOPE: voidObligation flow + option validation in the obligation ledger module.
NON_GOALS: No new transaction coordinator / journal unification unless achievable trivially through existing seams (guard + documented recovery beats building a protocol engine). registerRequest/request flows untouched.
VALIDATION: Negative tests: (a) void with no evidence journal configured => throws AND zero journal events persisted; (b) injected evidence-append failure after void event => reload reports voided_without_evidence reconciliation entry. bun test tests/obligation* then full suite.
source.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-08-27): Defect anchor is EXP/src/finalize/index.ts FinalizeController.voidObligation L216-254 (ledger.journal.append L233 BEFORE SettlementEvidenceEntrySchema.parse L243 / opts.evidence guard L244), not src/obligation/index.ts as originally written — obligation/index.ts sites cited were generic append + reconcileOnLoad backstop only. source.description:
PROBLEM: Channel-comm cursor seam violates the canonical cursor contract and cross-contaminates channels. getCursors/setCursors are keyed by participant_id only, values {last_read_seq,last_ack_seq} are participant-wide, while msg.seq is a CHANNEL-LOCAL display ordinal; inbox compares them directly (src/channel-comm/index.ts L126, L447) => participant reads channel A through seq 20, channel B seq 1..5 messages all appear already-read. Service comments admit seq is display-only and the real store needs channel_messages.id. Related: canSee returns true unconditionally for chain/node visibility (L188-196) because no membership model exists - tolerable only behind a guaranteed pre-scoped store, unsafe as the eventual production API.

SUCCESS: Cursor identity moved toward the canon NOW, preserving no intermediate abstraction: global channel_messages.id becomes the semantic read/ack cursor position (subscription.last_seen_id-style); seq demoted to display-only everywhere it is compared. Multi-channel correctness proven. Production visibility seam: either a membership resolver exists or the store/context construction makes foreign-container messages unsurfactable (the unconditional true case removed or provably unreachable).

SCOPE: src/channel-comm/* cursors/storage/visibility contracts + seam fixtures/tests. Store seam may gain message-id lookup; API docs updated to name the canon (channel_messages.id, subscription.last_seen_id, seq=display).
NON_GOALS: Scheduler/runtime integration stays xtrm-q99. Transport wire format beyond this module untouched.
VALIDATION: Regressions: (a) read A high-seq => B low-seq still unread; (b) chain-visible message inaccessible to non-member OR provably-scoped store construction asserted; single-channel suite stays green. bun test tests/channel-comm* then full suite.

source.description:
PROBLEM: Pure compiler emits its result under the name capability_grants (schema L105 CapabilityGrantSchema, operator allowlist intersection L178 allowed_tools, emission L233 resolveCapabilityGrants - src/chain-compiler/index.ts), but the value is only step-requests INTERSECT operator allowed_tools/allowed_skills: a compile-time upper bound. Accepted ADR-004 defines ResolvedCapabilityGrant as SpecialistDefinition requirements + chain/step policy + operator policy + runtime/sandbox availability. Compiler lacks resolved SpecialistDefinition, SpecialistActivationProfile, and real runtime/sandbox availability. Keeping the grandiose name invites q99 to treat compile-time allowlists as final grant authority and skip the sandbox half.

SUCCESS: Artifact renamed (preferred CompiledCapabilityBounds; PolicyAllowedRequests acceptable) across exports/schema/callers; doc comment states the bound nature, enumerates the missing ADR-004 inputs, and names PREPARE/ActivationSupervisor resolution as the completion point. q99-facing contract line recorded so runtime wiring cannot misread.

SCOPE: chain-compiler renames + dependent tests + short boundary doc. Run GitNexus impact before editing the renamed symbols (in-module rename expected).
NON_GOALS: NO partial ADR-004 implementation here; no ActivationProfile/PREPARE work (successor territory).
VALIDATION: Full bun test tests/ green after rename; grep confirms zero stale capability_grants references inside experiment src; detect_changes scope clean.
source.title: R6 Rename compiler capability_grants -> CompiledCapabilityBounds (ADR-004 boundary honesty)
